title: Alarchin Bridge / Rehabilitation
summary: Major rehabilitation design for a protected bridge crossing the Griboyedov Canal in Saint Petersburg.
methods: Finite-element analysis (PARIS) · rehabilitation design · steel / concrete · drawings
challenge: Develop a rehabilitation scheme for an existing heritage bridge while addressing structural performance, site constraints and conservation requirements.
approach: Developed structural models, examined the existing bridge configuration and designed rehabilitation interventions. Prepared calculation and drawing documentation.
outcome: Graduate qualification work defended with Excellent (A). The bridge also serves as a case study in lifecycle-management research.

title: Road Bridge Superstructure with an Orthotropic Deck / Design & Analysis
discipline: Steel bridge design · orthotropic deck · finite-element analysis
summary: Three bridge superstructure schemes were compared; the selected steel bridge uses four main I-girders and an orthotropic deck, with a 473.57 m total length and a (42.30 + 6 × 63.00 + 42.30 m) span arrangement.
role: Individual academic course project — bridge superstructure design and structural analysis.
methods: SOFiSTiK Structural Desktop / SOFiPLUS-X / ASE / MAXIMA / Eigenvalues / TEDDY · Microsoft Excel · BridgeInfluenceAreas · finite-element modelling · staged launching analysis.
challenge: Develop three alternative superstructure schemes for a road bridge with a 420 m navigable opening and two 60 × 10 m navigation clearances; select and develop one configuration for detailed design.
approach: Developed three schemes: a four-I-girder steel superstructure, a twin steel-box-girder alternative with reinforced-concrete approach spans, and a combined box-girder/arch scheme. Variant 1 was selected as the most economically advantageous. The selected scheme was developed through checks of the orthotropic deck, main girders, fatigue, serviceability, local stability, connections, bearings and expansion joints. Beam-grillage and shell finite-element models were built in SOFiSTiK; moving-load positioning and load processing used BridgeInfluenceAreas and Microsoft Excel. A separate construction-stage model examined longitudinal launching and natural vibration.
outcome: Variant 1 was selected as the most economically advantageous. The reported main-girder and orthotropic-deck strength and stability checks satisfy their stated resistance criteria. The separate launching analysis identifies a temporary-support requirement in span No. 7 and a first-mode period exceeding the stated limit at one launching position.

calculation_results.result: Temporary support required in span No. 7
calculation_results.location: The report states that the superstructure capacity is insufficient for launching-stage bending moments and calls for a more detailed check including longitudinal and transverse bracing.

calculation_note: The staged-launching analysis identifies two construction-stage findings: a first-mode period of 4.17 s at 293 m of launching, above the stated 3.00 s criterion, and the need for a temporary support in span No. 7 because of the launching-stage bending-moment demand. The report recommends a more detailed check including longitudinal and transverse bracing.
